name: POST /api/sla/alerts/dispatch - Retry undelivered SLA notifications
description: Re-attempts the outbound notification for every SLA alert still in the pending state, oldest first. A command that changes state without creating an addressable resource, so it answers 200 (MUST-54). This endpoint exists because the alert ROW is written before the notification is sent: the escalation is durable and visible in-app the moment it is raised, and the outbound send through ProjexCloud sdk-notification is a separate, retryable step. A gateway outage therefore degrades the CHANNEL rather than silencing the escalation, and this sweep drains the backlog once the gateway returns - which is exactly the guarantee a manager escalation needs. Each attempt uses the alert id as the idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout cannot deliver the same notification twice upstream. An alert that has exhausted its retry budget (attempts at or above the maximum) moves to failed and is skipped by later runs so a permanently undeliverable address cannot stall the queue; the row stays readable in-app. When the gateway is UNCONFIGURED the sweep is a deliberate no-op that leaves alerts pending rather than marking them delivered - claiming delivery no notification service ever saw would be a lie the audit trail could not detect. limit is clamped to 1..500 and defaults to 100. THE SWEEP IS BOUNDED BY THE CLOCK, NOT ONLY BY limit. Every attempt is a sequential network call through the composer, so a sweep of the default 100 against an unresponsive gateway took 36 SECONDS and answered long after every caller had given up - and the backlog is longest exactly when the gateway is worst, so the sweep gets slower the more it is needed. It now stops after 5 seconds and reports abandoned (rows it did not reach) and budget_exhausted. NOTHING IS LOST: unattempted alerts keep state:pending and their attempt count, and the next sweep takes them first because the query is oldest-first. abandoned is kept SEPARATE from failed because the two call for different responses - abandoned says sweep again, failed says fix the channel. THE COUNTERS ARE NOT ASSERTED AS EQUALITIES. attempted, delivered, failed and abandoned all depend on how much is pending in the target database and on whether ProjexCloud answers; pinning them (this definition previously pinned attempted:0) asserts the state of the environment rather than the behaviour of the endpoint, and MUST-61 rules it out. The happy path therefore asserts success:true - the 200-with-a-body contract - and the counters are documented here instead. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: Drain the pending notification backlog within the sweep budget
Reject a limit above the maximum

errorCases.when: limit is present and not an integer between 1 and 500
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
